subject: Private deployment: authorization matrix, customer keys, and third-party access
messages:
From: Sara Legal <sara.legal@acmecloud.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Procurement <mike.procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy questions — key control, subprocessors, and access matrix

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme Cloud is excited about the potential fit. Legal and security asked us to follow up with a few concrete items we need to resolve before the SOW:  

1) Custody of crypto keys: we understand Redwood offers customer-managed keys for Private deployments. Can you confirm which key managers are supported (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM) and whether Redwood ever has the ability to decrypt data when a customer key is used?

2) Operator/engineer access: we need an authorization matrix listing exactly which Redwood roles (if any) can access model artifacts, logs, or decrypted request payloads in a VPC-hosted Private deployment.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfers: please provide the current subprocessor roster for Private (including infra partners and monitoring agents) and whether any subprocessors are located outside the US. We also need an approach to getting 30-day notice for changes.

4) DPA language: attached is our proposed annotated DPA. We expect to keep customer keys customer-controlled, limit operator access to metadata-only unless break-glass is invoked, and require explicit audit logs for any emergency access. See the comments.

Can you get us an authorization matrix and a short note on key custody and access mechanics by EOD tomorrow? If helpful, I can set a quick call with our security lead.

Thanks —
Sara

--
Sara Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Cloud
Attachments: acme-dpa-annotated.docx (20KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Legal <sara.legal@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Mike Procurement <mike.procurement@acmecloud.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — key control, subprocessors, and access matrix

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the annotated DPA; we reviewed at a high level. Quick answers up front and we'll follow with the authorization matrix and a short architecture diagram.

1) Keys: Redwood Private supports AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer-provided HSMs (PKCS#11). When customer keys are configured in the keystore mode we do not hold the plaintext keys in our control plane. Redwood does not have the ability to decrypt request payloads protected by a customer-managed key unless a customer explicitly configures a break-glass procedure that grants us escrow access. We will document the exact handshake flows and relevant CSP integrations.

2) Operator access: by default operator roles see metrics, provisioning state, and encrypted storage objects only. No plaintext model input/output or decrypted artifacts are accessible to our operators in a standard deployment. Break-glass is an auditable, signed flow that requires two-person approval and is logged to the customer's audit storage. We'll provide the per-role matrix you requested.

3) Subprocessors: short answer — infra partners (public cloud IaaS for Dedicated bursts), telemetry vendors (self-hostable optional collector), and an observability agent (optional). For Private VPC/on-prem customers we minimize subprocessors; most telemetry agents are customer-deployed. We'll share a current roster and the notification cadence for changes (30 days notice is feasible; we can add contract language).

4) DPA: we can accept the proposed customer key language with minor edits around operational exceptions and break-glass. We'll attach a redwood-annotated DPA and an authorization matrix.

Action plan:
- I'm attaching a proposed authz matrix (proposed-authz-matrix.xlsx) and a short arch diagram (redwood-privdep-arch-diagram.pdf).
- Looping in Vivek to confirm the break-glass controls and audit log export options.

If you want a 30-minute call with our security engineering lead, we have availability tomorrow at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-authz-matrix.xlsx, redwood-privdep-arch-diagram.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deploy questions — key control, subprocessors, and access matrix

Priya / Lauren — forwarding Sara's thread and your draft responses. Notes from my review:

- Break-glass: we should specify cryptographic escrow only when requested and implemented via a customer-approved HSM-backed key-wrapping flow. No default escrow.
- Audit logs: we must ensure logs (operator sessions, GRPC call traces that contain metadata) are exported to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS) by default for Private. Retention policy should be definable per-customer.
- Subprocessors: compile a concise list: (1) Cloud infra for optional bursts: AWS, GCP; (2) Observability agent vendor: TraceSight (we offer a self-hosted collector as option); (3) Optional metrics aggregator used in Hosted mode only. For Private deployments, we only run a thin control plane with customer VPC peering — many of these subprocessors don't touch customer data.

I'll draft specific DPA wording around operator access and break-glass conditions. Priya — can you push the authz matrix with explicit role names (Support Engineer, Platform Operator, SRE, Security Ops) and the allowed actions (view provisioning state, view encrypted blobs, request break-glass, approve break-glass)? Use the proposed-authz-matrix.xlsx as the base.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Legal <sara.legal@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Mike Procurement <mike.procurement@acmecloud.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — key control, subprocessors, and access matrix

Sara — sending the materials Vivek and I discussed. Attached: redwood-privdep-arch-diagram.pdf (high level), proposed-authz-matrix.xlsx (role -> allowed actions), and redwood-annotated-dpa.docx with line edits keyed to your comments. Highlights / summary:  

- Customer key custody: Support for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and PKCS#11 HSMs. No Redwood access to plaintext when keys are configured in customer-keystore mode.
- Break-glass: only by explicit customer request; requires two internal Redwood approvers + customer-signed request. All break-glass operations are exported to customer-managed audit storage and include the exact justification and operator ids.
- Operator scope: default production operators can see provisioning state, queue metrics, and encrypted object references. No access to decrypted model inputs/outputs or customer plaintext.
- Subprocessors: attached roster (TraceSight, public cloud partners for burst capacity — which do not handle decrypted payloads in Private mode). We will contractually provide 30 days' notice for subprocessor additions.

Next steps: if this aligns, let's confirm the DPA edits and I can push a redline for signature. If Acme wants the break-glass escrow enabled in the SOW we can include an HSM-key-handoff appendix and an operator access addendum.

Would you like the security call tomorrow at 10:00 PT?

Thanks,
Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
